mechanism: Once-daily oral peptide dual GLP-1/GIP receptor agonist intended for obesity, overweight, and metabolic disease indications.
phase: Phase 2 oral tablet program; assigned NCT06506175 is Phase 1
development_status: The assigned NCT06506175 record is a Phase 1 China dosing-condition/food-effect pharmacokinetic study in healthy male volunteers and remains not yet recruiting with stale 2024 estimated dates. Related HRS9531 tablet studies include a completed Phase 1 SAD/MAD trial, a completed Phase 2 obesity trial, a recruiting Phase 1 relative-bioavailability study, and a not-yet-recruiting Phase 2 T2D trial. Kailera/Hengrui reported positive oral Phase 2 obesity topline data and stated that Hengrui plans China Phase 3 and Kailera plans a global Phase 2 trial in 2026.
clinical_summary: HRS9531 tablets are the oral formulation of ribupatide, a GLP-1/GIP receptor dual agonist peptide. The assigned NCT06506175 study focuses on AUCtau, Cmax, Tmax, half-life, anti-drug antibodies, and adverse events under different dosing, fasting, timing, and food conditions, not clinical efficacy. In the completed NCT06841445 Phase 2 obesity trial, Kailera/Hengrui reported mean weight loss up to 12.1% at Week 26 for once-daily oral ribupatide, with up to 38.6% of participants on 25 mg achieving at least 15% weight loss. A newly posted Phase 2 T2D tablet study will evaluate HbA1c, body weight, FPG, hypoglycemia, and adverse events through 2027.
safety_summary: Direct oral HRS9531 safety is early but generally class-consistent. A Phase 1 ADA poster reported all treatment-emergent adverse events in HRS9531 tablet groups were mild to moderate, with no serious adverse events or hypoglycemic episodes; common events included GI symptoms, hyperuricemia, hypertriglyceridemia, and nausea. In oral Phase 2 obesity topline results, Kailera/Hengrui reported most TEAEs were mild to moderate and GI-related, nausea of 11.9% to 22.7%, vomiting of 2.4% to 11.4%, and no permanent discontinuations or down-titrations due to nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or constipation. GLP-1 analog labeling supports monitoring for thyroid C-cell tumor boxed warning, pancreatitis, gallbladder disease, hypoglycemia with insulin or secretagogues, acute kidney injury from volume depletion, severe GI reactions, hypersensitivity, diabetic retinopathy, heart-rate increase, aspiration risk with anesthesia, pregnancy discontinuation, and delayed absorption of oral medications.
management_tools: Pharmacy benefit prior authorization with FDA-labeled indication, baseline BMI, weight-related comorbidity, and T2D documentation where applicable
Step therapy or preferred-agent sequencing against established GLP-1/GIP and GLP-1 products if clinically appropriate
Dose and quantity limits aligned to final tablet titration and maintenance schedule
Continuation criteria requiring clinically meaningful weight loss, HbA1c response for T2D, adherence, and tolerability
Requirements for reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity documentation consistent with obesity analog policies
Avoidance of concurrent GLP-1, GLP-1/GIP, or duplicate incretin products unless final labeling supports use

Monitoring for GI intolerance, dehydration/renal risk, pancreatitis symptoms, gallbladder disease, hypoglycemia when used with insulin or secretagogues, diabetic retinopathy history, and pregnancy plans
Administration counseling for empty-stomach morning dosing, water-only administration, and separation from food, beverages, or other oral medications if final label resembles oral semaglutide
evidence_gaps: The assigned NCT06506175 record has not been updated since July 2024 and remains not yet recruiting despite estimated 2024 start and completion dates.
No direct NCT06506175 results are posted.
No direct HRS9531 tablet U.S. trial, FDA-regulated study flag, filing plan, or U.S. launch timing was identified.
Oral Phase 2 obesity data are topline company-reported results; full peer-reviewed data were not identified.
The T2D tablet program is earlier than the obesity tablet study and the Phase 2 T2D trial is not yet recruiting as of the May 2026 ClinicalTrials.gov posting.
No direct HRS9531 tablet price is available; annual cost uses oral GLP-1 and obesity analog list prices.
Injectable HRS9531/ribupatide is substantially more advanced than the oral tablet formulation, so injectable timelines should not be treated as tablet launch timing.

expected_launch_window.method: Used the most advanced oral tablet status: completed China Phase 2 obesity trial, recruiting Phase 1 formulation study through September 2026, planned/not-yet-recruiting Phase 2 T2D study through July 2027, company-stated China Phase 3 and global Phase 2 plans, and absence of an identified U.S. tablet pivotal trial or filing.
expected_launch_window.explanation: The oral formulation has supportive early data but remains behind injectable ribupatide. A U.S. launch would require global Phase 2 execution, pivotal evidence, filing, and review, so 2030+ is a conservative monitoring estimate.

annual_cost_range.method: No direct HRS9531 tablet price was found. Low equals Rybelsus oral semaglutide list price analog: $997.58 per package x 12. High equals Wegovy oral obesity tablet list price analog: $1,349.02 per package x 12.
annual_cost_range.explanation: The range brackets an oral GLP-1 T2D tablet analog and an approved oral obesity GLP-1 tablet analog. It excludes rebates, discounts, self-pay programs, dispensing fees, monitoring, and any premium for dual GLP-1/GIP activity.

clinical_differentiation.method: Weighted oral dual GLP-1/GIP peptide mechanism, once-daily tablet route, Phase 2 obesity weight-loss signal, and early tolerability against limited duration, company-topline status, China-only direct efficacy data, and lack of U.S. pivotal tablet evidence.
clinical_differentiation.explanation: An oral dual incretin with double-digit 26-week weight loss could be clinically meaningful versus injectable-only dual agonists and oral GLP-1 monotherapy, but current evidence is not mature enough for a High rating.

budget_impact.method: Combined high chronic GLP-1 analog annual costs with very large obesity/T2D eligible populations and expected ongoing utilization pressure for oral options.
budget_impact.explanation: Even if net costs are below list, an effective oral dual incretin could materially expand demand among patients preferring tablets or avoiding injections. Broad chronic use makes budget exposure high.

disruption_risk.method: Balanced future oral dual-incretin differentiation and high demand against pre-pivotal U.S. status, crowded GLP-1 market, and payer experience managing obesity incretins with PA and quantity limits.
disruption_risk.explanation: If approved, the tablet could complicate sequencing, oral/injectable preference, and formulary contracting. Near-term disruption is moderated by the absence of a U.S. pivotal tablet program or filing.

recommended_action.method: Matched action to Phase 2 oral evidence, company-stated upcoming global Phase 2, no U.S. filing signal, no direct price, and stale assigned Phase 1 record.
recommended_action.explanation: Track full oral Phase 2 presentation, China Phase 3 start, global Phase 2 initiation, T2D tablet data, formulation/bioavailability results, and any U.S. regulatory or pricing signal.

quality_flags: Assigned NCT06506175 is stale: ClinicalTrials.gov lists not-yet-recruiting status with estimated 2024 start and completion dates and no update since July 17, 2024.
The packet aggregates the HRS9531 tablet program because the assigned record is a Phase 1 PK/dosing-condition study rather than the most advanced oral tablet efficacy study.
No direct U.S. HRS9531 tablet clinical trial, FDA-regulated study, regulatory filing, or U.S. launch date was identified.
No direct HRS9531 tablet price was found; annual cost range uses oral semaglutide analog list prices.
Company topline oral Phase 2 obesity data have not been replaced by a full peer-reviewed publication in the sources reviewed.
Injectable ribupatide/HRS9531 has later-stage evidence and China filing activity, but those milestones should not be assumed to apply to the oral tablet formulation.
